content.content:
# Mine

Mine is a set of PWAs (Progressive Web Apps) to digitalize ones personal or professional life.
The key idea is to save everything in a repo as markdown files. This can be calendar entries,
diaries, markdowns extracted from voice recordings / pdfs / .. These .md files can easily be
ported to new apps without a vendor lock-in and are processed via an (AI) assistant to help you
plan your day, keep track of tasks, remind you of memories a.k.a. a second brain.

To keep complexity to a minimum each use-case lives in a separate folder. e.g. the calendar PWA
lives completely in a 'calendar' folder as does the zettelkasten and all the other apps. Each
folder contains a 'sample' folder with samples how the markdowns shall look, a REQUIREMENTS.md
describing how the PWA works and a TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md describing how it is built.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for how this is built.

## One app, one setup

Mine installs as **one** app on the phone, with one icon. The apps in the subfolders are pages
inside it, not separate installs.

This is what makes the central requirement work: **the GitHub repo and token are entered once,
in the main app, and every app in a subfolder uses them.** Verified on iPhone and Android.

## Main app

A tile per app: its `icon.svg` above its folder name.

Above the tiles, apps may contribute a summary. The calendar's shows today's entries and the
next one — which matters, because opening the app is the only reminder that works (see below).

## First run

1. Open the app URL and add it to the home screen (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen;
   Android: menu → Install).
2. The setup screen asks for GitHub owner, data repo, branch, and a personal access token.
3. The app tests the connection and reports clearly if it fails.

Settings are stored on the device only. The token is never displayed again after entry, and the
app warns 14 days before it expires.

## Using it

- Changes appear instantly and are queued for GitHub in the background.
- A sync indicator shows: in sync / pending / error.
- Offline, the queue is kept and sent when you are back online or reopen the app.
- Editing the same entry on two devices never loses either version: the other device's version
  keeps the file, yours is kept beside it, and the app asks which to keep.
- Everything works offline, including dates and search, because the app keeps a full local copy.

## Reminders

**Mine cannot notify you while it is closed.** No browser can schedule a notification for later;
this is a platform limitation, not a missing feature. Alerts are stored with each entry and
exported, and they fire while the app is open. The summary on the tile screen is the reminder.

## Updates

When a new version is deployed the app shows "Update ready — reload". It never updates while you
are in the middle of editing.

## Privacy

Your data lives in a **private** repo. The app itself is public, but it contains no data, and the
token is scoped so that it can only touch the data repo.

content.content:
===== REQUIREMENTS.md =====
# Calendar

Calendar is an app of [Mine](../REQUIREMENTS.md) to manage your calendar. Every entry is one
markdown file in the data repo, so your calendar stays readable and portable without this app.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for the file format.

## What an entry holds

A title, a type — **event** or **task** — a start and end, a group, a location, participants,
alerts, and a free markdown body for the agenda, checklist or notes.

A task can be ticked done. An event cannot. Entries can repeat, and a repeating entry can have
single occurrences skipped, moved or ticked off without affecting the rest.

## Layout

A navigation pane at the top and a big calendar window below it.

In the top pane, from left to right:

- Left/right buttons to move to the previous/next day, week, month or year, depending on the
  current view.
- The current day/week/month/year, with a small downward arrow for a dropdown date picker. The
  dropdown shows a month at a time, with its name top left and left/right arrows top right.
  Clicking the month name switches to a year grid of 9 years ending with the current one, whose
  arrows page by 9 years.
- A dropdown to choose the view: day, week, month or year.
- A dropdown to filter by group. Each group shows its colour; double-clicking one lets you edit
  its label and colour.

All views show **7 columns, Monday to Sunday**, with weekends tinted so the work week still
reads as a block. A Saturday task has to be visible.

## Views

- **Year** — every month, each with a `M T W T F S S` header row and one row per week. The
  current day is highlighted. A day with entries takes the background colour of its group, split
  between colours if there are several. Clicking a day shows that day's entries. Groups switched
  off in the filter are not shown.
- **Month** — one row per week. Entries appear as rows inside each day cell, sorted by time, all
  day items first. Tasks have a rectangular icon on the right to tick them done. Clicking empty
  space in a cell creates an entry; clicking an entry opens it.
- **Week** — columns are the days, rows are the 24 hours.
- **Day** — the week view for a single day, with more detail per entry.

## Entry popup

A title row; below it a button group to choose the type; below that the remaining fields; below
those an auto-growing monospace box holding the markdown body. A `discard` and a `save` button
at the bottom.

The body is written and shown as raw markdown, so what you see is exactly what lands in the file.

## On a phone

The views above describe the desktop. On a phone a month cell is about 50px wide, so entry rows
are neither readable nor tappable. The same screens adapt:

- The top pane collapses to `[<] [April 2026 v] [=]`.
- Month and year cells show group-coloured dots instead of rows of text.
- Tapping a day opens a sheet listing that day's entries, each one tappable, with an
  `+ add entry` button — so nothing is ever smaller than a finger.

## On the main screen

The tile screen of the main app shows today's entries and the next one coming up.
===== TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md =====
# Calendar — technical requirements

File format and rendering for [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md). Sync, caching and writes are
in [../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Paths

```
calendar/2026/04/2026-04-18-1400-k3f9.md     one-off entry
calendar/2026/04/2026-04-25-0000-ov1q.md     occurrence override
calendar/recurring/trash-p7qm.md             entry with a recurrence rule
calendar/groups.md                           group -> colour and label
```

The whole folder is mirrored locally, so the path is not a loading optimisation. It is for
humans: the repo browses chronologically on github.com, and no directory grows past a month of
entries. `-k3f9` is 4 random characters, **not** a counter — two devices creating entries offline
on the same day must never mint the same name. No title slug, so retitling is never a rename.

**The path is never the source of truth.** It is derived from `start` at creation; after a move
or an override the two can disagree. Always read `start`. Changing an entry's date is a rename,
which is a delete plus a create in one commit.

Entries with a `recurrence:` rule live in `recurring/` rather than the date tree, because an
open-ended rule must render in months it was not created in and there is no month folder to find
it under.

## Frontmatter

RFC 5545 (iCalendar) naming wherever one exists, so `.ics` export is close to a field copy.
**Empty keys are omitted, never written as `None`** — `None` is a YAML string, not null, and a
parser hands back the text `"None"`.

| Key | Applies to | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | both | required |
| `type` | both | `event` or `task` |
| `start` | both | `DTSTART`. A bare date (`2026-04-18`) is all-day; a timestamp (`2026-04-18T14:00:00Z`) is an instant |
| `end` | both | same value types as `start`; omitted when a single all-day item |
| `group` | both | a name, resolved through `groups.md` |
| `done` | `task` only | `true` / `false` |
| `location` | both | free text |
| `alerts` | both | minutes before start, `0` = at start. Stored and exported only; nothing fires in the background |
| `participants` | both | list of email addresses |
| `recurrence` | both | RRULE string, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SA` |
| `exdate` / `rdate` | recurring | occurrences to skip / extra occurrences |
| `series` | override | id of the recurring file it belongs to |
| `recurrence-id` | override | the original occurrence date this file replaces |
| `conflictOf` | conflict file | written by sync |

No `duration` key — it is `end - start`.

Type and time are independent: `type` decides whether the entry can be ticked done, the value
type of `start` decides whether it is all-day or timed. A task is usually all-day, but may carry
a time and then renders at it.

The bare-date form matters. An all-day task stored as `2026-04-18T00:00:00Z` lands on the wrong
day outside UTC and shifts twice a year on DST.

The markdown body is the entry's content and is preserved byte-for-byte by anything that does not
explicitly edit it.

## Overrides

A recurring file states the rule only. Anything that happens to a *single* occurrence — ticked,
moved, retitled, cancelled — is an override file in the date tree carrying `series:` and
`recurrence-id:`, holding only the keys that differ. The rule file is never rewritten, and since
each override is a fresh path it cannot conflict, even when two devices do it offline.

`exdate:` covers a plain skip where there is nothing to record.

## Rendering a range

1. Collect dated entries whose `start` falls in the range.
2. Expand every rule in `recurring/` over the range; drop dates in `exdate`, add `rdate`.
3. Replace an occurrence with the override matching `series` + `recurrence-id`; an override
   marked cancelled removes it.
4. Drop groups switched off in the filter.
5. Sort: all-day first, then by start time.

Index overrides by `` `${series}|${recurrenceId}` `` once per load; a linear scan per occurrence
is what makes month views slow.

## RRULE

Full RRULE on read — files may be hand-written or imported. The UI only *writes* daily / weekly /
monthly / yearly with `INTERVAL`, `BYDAY`, `UNTIL`, `COUNT`.

`rrule.js` works in UTC. For an all-day rule, set `DTSTART` to UTC midnight and read only the
year/month/day back, never `getDate()` on a local Date — east of UTC that returns the previous
day. `UNTIL` must be written in the `Z` form.

## Groups

`groups.md` is a markdown file whose frontmatter maps a group name to a colour and a label. An
entry stores the name, so recolouring or relabelling is a one-file edit instead of a rewrite of
every entry, and there is no cap on the number of groups. Unknown group renders grey. It lives in
the data repo, so the mapping follows you across devices.

## Widget

`widget.js` exports `summary()`, returning today's entries and the next upcoming one for the main
app's tile screen.

# Mine — technical requirements

How [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) is built. Everything here was verified against the live
API or on device on 2026-11-19; `spike/` re-runs the device checks and needs no token.

## Repos

| Repo | Visibility | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maximilianharr/mine` | public | this app, served by Pages at `/mine/` |
| `maximilianharr/mine-data` | **private** | the markdown data |

Pages cannot serve a private repo without Enterprise, so data in the app repo would be
world-readable at a predictable URL. The token is scoped to the data repo only.

## Layout

One `manifest.json` with `scope: /mine/`, one service worker at the root. Subfolders are ordinary
pages inside that scope. `/mine/` and `/mine/calendar/` are the same origin, so they share one
IndexedDB — that is the whole mechanism behind "enter the token once".

```
/index.html /manifest.json /sw.js
/shared/  apps.js  store.js  github.js  md.js  vendor/
/calendar/  index.html  app.js  widget.js  icon.svg  sample/
```

No build step: no bundler, no CI, no node_modules. `git push` deploys, every page opens from
disk, all paths relative so the `/mine/` prefix needs no config.

`shared/apps.js` exports the app list and is imported by both the tile screen and `sw.js`, so
adding an app means editing one array. An app may export `summary()` from `widget.js`.

## Bootstrap — 1 request

One GraphQL query returns an app folder's tree **with contents and blob SHAs**, nested to the
depth of the layout:

```graphql
repository(owner:$o, name:$r) { object(expression:"main:calendar") {
  ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
    ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
      ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
        ... on Blob { oid text isTruncated } } } } } } } } } } }
```

- `rateLimit.cost` is **1** however many files return — `entries` is not a paginated connection.
  A 16 MB / 145 file response came back in 6 s without error.
- `Blob.oid` is byte-identical to the REST tree SHA, so this single request also supplies the
  SHAs that pulls diff against and writes send as their base.
- Check `isTruncated`: GraphQL truncates very large blobs and returns `text: null` for binary.
  Fall back to a REST blob fetch for that path.
- An **empty repo** returns `object: null` rather than an error, and `defaultBranchRef: null`.
  Treat it as an empty mirror, not a failure.

**Do not use the tarball.** `GET /tarball/{ref}` 302-redirects to `codeload.github.com`, which
answers `access-control-allow-origin: https://render.githubusercontent.com` — one specific
foreign origin. `fetch()` applies CORS to the final response after the redirect, so it is
blocked, and the preflight an authenticated request needs returns 403. `api.github.com/graphql`
by contrast sends `allow-origin: *` and a 204 preflight allowing `Authorization`.

**A repo with no commits rejects the Git Data API outright.** Not just the ref read — `POST
/git/blobs` itself answers 409 "Git Repository is empty", so there is nothing to build a tree
from. Only `PUT /contents/{path}` can create the first commit. The first queued file goes that
way, and everything after drains normally once a history exists.

## Pull

1. `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{branch}` with `If-None-Match`. A 304 means nothing changed and
   costs no rate-limit quota.
2. On 200: fetch the tree, diff blob SHAs, fetch only changed files, drop deleted paths.

Run on app open and on window focus. Background Sync does not exist in Safari, so all syncing is
foreground.

## Writes — one commit per drain

Queue each change locally with the blob SHA it was based on, then drain the whole queue as one
commit via the Git Data API: `POST /git/blobs` per file, `POST /git/trees` with `base_tree`
(deletion = entry with `sha: null`), `POST /git/commits`, `PATCH /git/refs/heads/{branch}` with
the expected old SHA and **no force**.

One drain is one commit, so a move — delete plus create, because the date is in the path and the
API has no rename — cannot be half-applied, and a 20-item offline backlog is one commit.

A rejected ref update means someone pushed elsewhere: pull, rebuild on the new base, retry. This
succeeds, because nearly every write is a create at a freshly generated path.

**True conflict** = a queued change whose base SHA no longer matches the remote blob. Remote keeps
the canonical path; the local version is committed beside it as `<name>.conflict-<yyyymmdd>.md`
with `conflictOf:`. Nothing is discarded and the queue never jams. On 401/403, pause and send the
user to settings.

## Service worker

Registered `{type: 'module'}` so it can import `shared/apps.js`. A version constant names the
cache; install precaches the shell. Same-origin requests are cache-then-revalidate.

Requests to `api.github.com` **bypass the worker entirely** — caching an API response would hand
back a stale ETag and silently break sync.

A new worker waits; the UI offers "Update ready — reload" and `skipWaiting()` runs only on tap.

## Token and CSP

Stored plaintext in IndexedDB with its expiry: as safe as the unlocked device. The threat that
matters is injected script on our own origin, closed off by policy rather than encryption:

```
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com
```

**No CDNs, ever.** Dependencies are committed to `/shared/vendor/`, pinned by hand, with source
URL and version in `VENDOR.md`. The token is never written to a log, a URL, or the DOM.

The OAuth device flow is not an option: GitHub's `login/device/code` endpoints send no CORS
headers, so a fine-grained PAT is the only no-backend path.

## Dependencies

| What | Why not hand-rolled |
| --- | --- |
| `js-yaml` | Files are hand-edited and must parse as real YAML — quoting, multiline scalars, flow maps. A subset parser misreads them silently. |
| `rrule` | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR` and DST-crossing weeklies are where hand-rolled expansion is wrong without telling you. |

YAML *writing* is ours (~20 lines): we control the output shape, so no dumper is needed.

**Load with `CORE_SCHEMA`, never js-yaml's default.** The default is YAML 1.1 and parses
`start: 2026-04-18` into a JS Date at UTC midnight — silently shifting every all-day entry by a
day east of UTC. `CORE_SCHEMA` keeps it a string and still handles bools, numbers, flow maps and
quoted scalars. This is the same off-by-one the bare-date format exists to prevent, arriving
through the parser instead.

## Platform findings

Verified in both installed home-screen apps (iPhone/Safari, Pixel/Chrome); screenshots in
`spike/res/`.

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Storage shared across paths | **Yes.** A marker written by `/mine/spike/` was read back byte-identical by `/mine/spike/sub/`, both reporting `STANDALONE`. Cross-path module imports work too. |
| `{type:'module'}` service worker | Registers on Safari as well as Chrome. No classic fallback needed. |
| `storage.persisted()` | **Already granted**, no prompt, on both. An installed app is exempt from the ~7-day eviction that applies to uninstalled sites, so the token and mirror survive idle periods. |
| Quota | 35 GB (iPhone), 56 GB (Pixel), against a mirror measured in single-digit MB. |

Not tested, and no longer relevant: whether separately-installed PWAs get isolated storage. That
expectation is why the one-app topology was chosen.

Re-run `spike/` after a major iOS release — two of the four results above contradicted the
documented platform behaviour, and that is exactly the kind of thing that regresses silently.

content.text:
I've read `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md`, `calendar/*` and the samples. Before touching the doc, some context on what I found:

**Only the month view exists in code** (`calendar/app.js` renders `monthCells` and nothing else), so D/M/Y/K means building three new views plus kanban.

**Nine real contradictions** with the current spec, which I'll walk through one at a time:
1. Kanban's three states vs the data model's single `done:` boolean — and `status:` is already taken by `cancelled` overrides
2. Sprint number vs `start`/`end` as the source of truth for an item's date
3. D/M/Y/K drops the **week** view, which `REQUIREMENTS.md` specifies in detail
4. `start week on (sunday)` vs "All views show **7 columns, Monday to Sunday**, with weekends tinted"
5. `time zone (UTC+x)` vs the whole UTC-instant/bare-date design
6. Month cells showing titled lines vs "a month cell is about 50px wide, so entry rows are neither readable nor tappable"
7. The repeat dropdown has no *daily*, no *until/count*, and cannot express rules the format promises to read (`FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR`)
8. The icon toolbar has no home for `alerts`, `participants` or a task's done state
9. `priority`, `estimate`, `sprint`, `assignee` are four fields that don't exist in the format

Plus two truncated lines ("items can be dr", "on mobile shows the '") and the "update ready" item, which may need no requirements change at all.

Starting with the one everything else depends on:

content.text:
**Q1 → `stage:` replaces `done:`.** One field, and the month-view tick toggles todo↔done.

Next, the one that decides whether the kanban is a view or a second source of truth:

questions.question: You want a sprint number on each card, and "if an item is moved to another sprint then the start/end day are those of the sprint". Settings also give `kanban interval (x weeks)` and `kanban first week start date`, which together make sprint ↔ date-range a pure calculation. So should `sprint` be stored in the file, or derived from `start`?

options.label: Derived from `start` (Recommended)
options.description: No `sprint:` key. Sprint 7 = anchor + 6×interval weeks; a card's sprint is whichever range its `start` falls in. Moving to another sprint writes `start`/`end` only — which is exactly what you described, so the number can never disagree with the date. Consequence: the anchor and interval must live in the data repo, not on the device, or two phones put the same card in different sprints.

aiTitle: Task event popup and calendar fixes

content.text:
**Q4 → D W M Y K.** Five views.

Now the one I think is an outright bug if taken literally:

questions.question: Settings list `time zone (UTC+x)`. But a fixed UTC offset cannot represent a real zone across DST: 14:00 Berlin is `12:00Z` in July and `13:00Z` in January, so a fixed `UTC+1` renders every summer event an hour early — the exact class of off-by-one that `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md` spends three paragraphs guarding against. What should the setting actually be?

options.label: IANA zone name, default = device (Recommended)
options.description: Pick `Europe/Berlin`, not `UTC+1`. `Intl.DateTimeFormat` resolves the real offset per date, so DST is correct and no conversion code is hand-written. Default is the device's own zone, so it behaves exactly as today until you change it. Gives you a deliberate override — e.g. keeping home time while travelling.
options.preview:
Time zone  [ Europe/Berlin        v ]
           (device: Europe/Berlin)

stored:  start: 2026-07-18T12:00:00Z
shows:   14:00   (CEST, +2)

stored:  start: 2026-01-18T13:00:00Z
shows:   14:00   (CET, +1)

# all-day entries: never converted

options.label: No setting — always the device zone
options.description: Drop the row. Timed entries render wherever the phone says it is, which is right the moment you land somewhere. Smallest code, zero new failure modes, matches what the app does today. Cost: no way to keep the calendar in home time while abroad.
options.preview:
# settings row removed

stored:  start: 2026-07-18T12:00:00Z
shows:   14:00 in Berlin
         08:00 in New York
         (follows the device)

options.label: Fixed UTC+x offset, as written
options.description: A plain integer offset applied to every timed entry. Simple to store and show. Cost: every entry is off by an hour for roughly half the year in any DST zone, and the error is silent — you only notice by missing a meeting.

**Q10 → ten icons; "D" is the markdown body alone; stage is a segmented control under the title.**

Every popup has trash/x/disk, which raises what those mean on a *sub*-popup:

questions.question: "all popups have a trashcan to delete, an x to discard and a disk to save." On the entry popup those are clear — delete the entry, discard edits, write the file. On a sub-popup (location, repeat, category, alerts) they're ambiguous: does its disk write to the repo, or just commit the value into the entry form? Note a brand-new entry has no file yet, so a sub-popup has nothing to write to.

options.label: Sub-popups stage only (Recommended)
options.description: A sub-popup's disk commits the value into the open entry form and lights its icon; its trash clears that one field; its x abandons the sub-edit. Nothing reaches the repo until the entry popup's own disk. The entry popup's x therefore discards the staged location too, and its trash deletes the whole entry. Works identically for a new and an existing entry.
options.preview:
Location popup
  [ Room 3B                  ]
  [trash]        [x]  [disk]
    |             |     |
    |             |     +-> form.location = "Room 3B"
    |             |         pin icon lights up
    |             +-------> close, no change
    +---------------------> form.location = none

entry popup [disk] -> one commit
entry popup [x]    -> all of it dropped

options.label: Sub-popups write immediately
options.description: Each sub-popup's disk writes and pushes that field on its own. You never lose a field edit by closing the parent. Cost: a new entry must be auto-created on the first sub-popup save, so abandoning a half-made entry leaves an untitled file in the repo, and one entry edit becomes five commits.

  -> write calendar/2026/11/....md
  -> drain -> commit

new entry, no title yet:
  -> must create the file first
  -> [x] on the entry popup leaves
     an "(untitled)" file behind

options.label: Sub-popups stage; no trash on them
options.description: Same as the recommended option, but a sub-popup has only x and disk — clearing a field is done with the trashcan on its detail row at the bottom of the entry popup, which you already specified. One less button and no duplicate way to clear. Cost: not literally "all popups have a trashcan".

content.text:
**Q11 → sub-popups stage into the form; one commit on the entry popup's disk.**

Backgrounding the push moves error reporting out of the popup:

questions.question: Saving takes seconds because `commit()` in `calendar/app.js` awaits `drain()` — five sequential GitHub calls — before closing the popup. The main `REQUIREMENTS.md` already promises "Changes appear instantly and are queued for GitHub in the background", so the current behaviour contradicts it. But errors go into `#f-msg` inside the popup today; with the popup gone they need a home. Related: `REQUIREMENTS.md` says a conflict means "the app asks which to keep", while `drain()` actually resolves it silently — remote keeps the path, yours is committed beside it as `.conflict-YYYYMMDD.md`.

options.label: Sync line reports both (Recommended)
options.description: The popup closes the moment the local write lands; `drain()` runs unawaited. Push failures and conflicts both surface in the calendar's existing sync line, with conflicts as a tappable banner listing the kept-beside files. `REQUIREMENTS.md` is corrected to describe what the code does — nothing is discarded, and you review afterwards — rather than promising a prompt that never appears.
options.preview:
save -> popup closes, calendar visible

  in sync
  1 change pending
  push failed: Token rejected (401)
  1 conflict - both kept, review >

# REQUIREMENTS.md amended:
# "never loses either version; yours
#  is kept beside theirs and flagged"
# (was: "the app asks which to keep")

options.label: Sync line, and build the prompt
options.description: Same instant close, but a conflict genuinely asks which version to keep — honouring `REQUIREMENTS.md` as written. Cost: a real diff/choose UI, and the prompt has to appear long after you left the popup, possibly while you are editing something else.
options.preview:
save -> popup closes

  ... 4s later ...

  +----------------------------------+
  | "Weekly Sync" changed elsewhere  |
  |  [ keep theirs ] [ keep mine ]   |
  +----------------------------------+

# interrupts whatever you're doing now

options.label: Close instantly, stay quiet
options.description: Popup closes, push runs in the background, and only the pending counter reflects it. A failed push stays queued and retries on next focus, exactly like the offline path. Cost: a 401 from an expired token is invisible until you look at the sync line — you'd believe your edits were pushed.

save -> popup closes

  1 change pending

# retries on next focus
# no error text anywhere
# expired token = silent backlog

The kanban card needs four fields that don't exist in the format:

questions.question: Kanban cards show priority (1 red / 2 orange / 3 yellow), an estimate in days, and filter by "category, assignee, priority". None of these keys exist. RFC 5545 — which `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md` says to follow "wherever one exists" — has `PRIORITY` (1–9, 1 highest) but nothing for an estimate, and its people field is `ATTENDEE`, which the format already calls `participants`. How should these be named?

options.label: priority + estimate; assignee reuses participants (Recommended)
options.description: `priority: 1|2|3` is RFC 5545 `PRIORITY` — the UI writes only 1–3, but 1–9 is read from imported files and bucketed into the three colours. `estimate: 2` is days, non-standard and documented as such. "Assignee" filters on the existing `participants` list, so there is no second people-field to keep in sync. Both keys absent means no priority chip and no estimate shown.

questions.question: "in the popup add a '+ add' to add a category". `groups.md` stores three things per group: a **name** (what entries store in `group:`), a **label** and a **colour** — the split exists so recolouring or relabelling is a one-file edit instead of rewriting every entry. What does "+ add" ask for? Also, `REQUIREMENTS.md` currently says you edit a group by *double-clicking* it in the filter dropdown, which your pen-button convention would replace.

options.label: Label + colour; name is derived (Recommended)
options.description: Two fields. The name is slugged from the label at creation (`Sport & Doctor` → `sport-doctor`) and never shown in the UI. Editing moves to a pen button in the settings Groups list; double-click-to-edit is removed from `REQUIREMENTS.md`. Relabelling later does not change the name, so no entry is ever rewritten — which is the point of the split. Deleting a group leaves its entries rendering grey.

**Q18 → label + colour; name derived; pen replaces double-click.**

Two left. The update banner:

questions.question: I could not pin the "Update ready" bug down by reading `app.js` and `sw.js` — `registerSW()` offers the banner whenever `reg.waiting && navigator.serviceWorker.controller`, which is true for *any* waiting worker, including one byte-identical to the active one. That's a code fix either way. The question for the doc is whether the requirement itself should change: `REQUIREMENTS.md` currently just says 'When a new version is deployed the app shows "Update ready — reload"', which has no testable condition.

options.label: Make the condition testable (Recommended)
options.description: The requirement becomes: the banner appears only when a waiting worker reports a `VERSION` different from the active one, and never otherwise. `sw.js` already has `VERSION = '2026-11-19.3'`; the worker answers a version query, and the UI compares. Gives the fix a success criterion you can check, rather than "it shouldn't show when it shouldn't".
options.preview:
sw.js
  VERSION = '2026-11-19.3'
  onmessage 'version' -> reply VERSION

app.js
  active.version  = '2026-11-19.3'
  waiting.version = '2026-11-19.3'
  -> equal, no banner

  waiting.version = '2026-11-20.1'
  -> differs, show banner

success criterion: reload twice with
no deploy in between -> no banner

options.label: No requirements change — just fix the code
options.description: `REQUIREMENTS.md` stays as written; the banner logic is corrected as a bug with no doc change. Smallest edit to the spec. Cost: the requirement still has no condition anyone can test against, so the same bug can come back unnoticed.
options.preview:
REQUIREMENTS.md: unchanged

"When a new version is deployed the
 app shows 'Update ready - reload'."

# fix tracked as a bug only

options.label: Drop the banner — update on next cold open
options.description: No banner at all. A waiting worker activates the next time the app is opened fresh, never while it is on screen, so a false positive is impossible by construction. Cost: you cannot take an update without closing the app, and "It never updates while you are in the middle of editing" becomes the whole mechanism.
options.preview:

"A new version installs in the
 background and takes effect the next
 time the app is opened fresh. It

cd /home/max/ws/mine/calendar && cat > REQUIREMENTS.md <<'EOF'
# Calendar

Calendar is an app of [Mine](../REQUIREMENTS.md) to manage your calendar. Every entry is one
markdown file in the data repo, so your calendar stays readable and portable without this app.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for the file format.

## What an entry holds

A title, a type — **event** or **task** — a start and end, a group, a location, participants,
alerts, and a free markdown body for the agenda, checklist or notes.

A task also carries a **stage** — `todo`, `doing` or `done` — and, optionally, a priority (1, 2
or 3) and an estimate in days. An event has none of the three. Stage is the only record of a
task's progress; there is no separate done flag.

Entries can repeat, and a repeating entry can have single occurrences skipped, moved, retitled
or moved to another stage without affecting the rest.

## Layout

A navigation pane at the top and a big calendar window below it.

In the top pane, from left to right:

- Left/right buttons to move to the previous/next day, week, month, year or sprint, depending on
  the current view.
- The current day/week/month/year, with a small downward arrow for a dropdown date picker. The
  dropdown shows a month at a time, with its name top left and left/right arrows top right.
  Clicking the month name switches to a year grid of 9 years ending with the current one, whose
  arrows page by 9 years. In the kanban view the label reads `Sprint 7 · 19 Jan – 1 Feb` and the
  dropdown picks a sprint.
- A button to jump to today.
- A dropdown to filter by group. Each group shows its colour. This is a view filter and is
  remembered per device; groups are *named and coloured* in settings, not here.
- `D` `W` `M` `Y` `K` to choose the view: day, week, month, year, kanban.
- A return arrow back to the Mine tile screen.
- A gear button that opens settings.

All views show **seven columns beginning with the configured first day of the week**, with
Saturday and Sunday tinted wherever they land. A Saturday task has to be visible.

When *show calendar weeks* is on, each week row carries its ISO 8601 week number in a left
gutter, separated from the days by a thin vertical rule. The number is always ISO, whichever
day the week is set to start on.

A `+` button adds an entry. It defaults to today when today is in view, and otherwise to the
first day on screen — in the kanban, to the first day of the selected sprint, in its todo
column.

## Views

- **Year** — every month, each with a weekday header row and one row per week. The current day
  is highlighted. A day with entries takes the background colour of its group, split between
  colours if there are several — a year grid has no room for anything else. Clicking a day shows
  that day's entries.
- **Month** — one row per week. Entries appear inside each day cell as small lines carrying the
  title on the group's background colour, sorted by time, all-day items first. A cell shows at
  most four on desktop and two on a phone, then `+N`. Tasks have a rectangular icon on the right
  to move them straight to done. Clicking empty space in a cell creates an entry; clicking an
  entry opens it.
- **Week** — columns are the days, rows are the 24 hours.
- **Day** — the week view for a single day, with more detail per entry.
- **Kanban** — below.

Groups switched off in the filter are not shown in any view.

### The day preview

Clicking a day opens that day's entries as a list, each one tappable. Its top right carries a
small `+` to add an entry on that day and a small `x` to close it — not full-width buttons.

## Entry popup

A row of icon buttons at the top, from left to right:

- `T` for task, `E` for event. Choosing one deselects the other; the default is event.
- A circular-arrows button for **repetition**.
- A ball for **category**.
- A pin for **location**.
- A bell for **alerts**.
- A person for **participants**.
- `D` for **details** — the markdown body.
- Then, right-aligned: an `x` to close and discard, a trashcan to delete the entry, and a disk
  to save it.

An icon whose field is set is shown enabled: a brighter background in dark mode, a darker one in
light mode. So the row doubles as a summary of what the entry carries.

Each of the seven field buttons opens its own popup, and every popup has the same three buttons:
a trashcan that clears that one field, an `x` that abandons the sub-edit, and a disk that commits
the value into the entry form and lights the icon. **A sub-popup never writes to the repo.**
Nothing is written until the entry popup's own disk, so one entry edit is one commit, and the
entry popup's `x` discards the staged fields along with everything else. This is also what makes
a brand-new entry work, since it has no file for a sub-popup to write to.

Below the icon row:

- the title field;
- for a task, a `todo` / `doing` / `done` button group;
- the start and end fields;
- then one row per field that is set, in the order of the icons above — so a location that has
  been given appears at the bottom. Each row has a pen to reopen its popup and a trashcan to
  clear it.

Saving **closes the popup and returns to the calendar immediately**; the push to GitHub runs in
the background and is reported in the sync line, not in the popup.

### Repetition

A dropdown, not an RRULE field:

```
does not repeat · daily · weekly · every 2 weeks ·
monthly on the x-th · monthly on the x-th weekday · yearly
```

below it an **ends** control: never, on a date, or after a number of occurrences.

Files may be hand-written or imported, so a rule the dropdown cannot express — `the last Friday
of the month`, `Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays` — is shown as a non-selectable **custom** state
displaying the rule as text, with a note that choosing an option will replace it. Saving the
entry without touching the dropdown leaves the rule untouched. No hand-written rule is ever
silently rewritten.

### Category

The groups, each with its colour, and a `+ add` button. Adding a group asks for a label and a
colour; its stored name is derived from the label and never shown, which is why relabelling or
recolouring later touches no entry. A pen edits a group, a trashcan deletes it — and entries
still naming a deleted group render grey.

## Kanban

Three columns — **todo** (red), **doing** (yellow), **done** (green) — holding one sprint's
tasks. Every task is a card and every card is a task; events never appear.

A sprint is a date range, not a stored field: sprint 1 starts on the *kanban first week start
date* and each one runs for the *kanban interval*. A task's sprint is whichever range its start
falls in, so the number can never disagree with the date, and moving a card to another sprint
is exactly a change of its start and end. Both settings therefore live in the data repo, not on
the device — if they differed between two devices the same card would be in different sprints.

A repeating task contributes one card per occurrence inside the sprint. Moving one records an
override for that occurrence alone; the rule itself is never rewritten.

Each column header shows its state, its colour and a card count. The sprint selector and a
filter icon (category, assignee, priority) sit in the top pane, because one board shows one
sprint.

A card shows:

- a top row with a trashcan to delete, a pen to edit, the title, and `<` `>` to move it to the
  previous or next stage — `<` disabled in todo, `>` disabled in done;
- below it two lines of the markdown body;
- on the right a priority chip (1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow), the estimate in days, and the sprint

## What an entry holds

A title, a type — **event** or **task** — a start and end, a group, a location, participants,
alerts, and a free markdown body for the agenda, checklist or notes.

or 3) and an estimate in days. An event has none of the three. Stage is the only record of a
task's progress; there is no separate done flag.

Entries can repeat, and a repeating entry can have single occurrences skipped, moved, retitled
or moved to another stage without affecting the rest.

## Layout

A navigation pane at the top and a big calendar window below it.

In the top pane, from left to right:

- Left/right buttons to move to the previous/next day, week, month, year or sprint, depending on
  the current view.

Saturday and Sunday tinted wherever they land. A Saturday task has to be visible.

gutter, separated from the days by a thin vertical rule. The number is always ISO, whichever
day the week is set to start on.

first day on screen — in the kanban, to the first day of the selected sprint, in its todo
column.

| yearly | `FREQ=YEARLY` |
| ends on a date | `+UNTIL=<date>Z` |
| ends after n | `+COUNT=<n>` |

"""## Settings

Two of the settings are data, not preferences, and live in `calendar/settings.md`:

---
```

| `start` | both | `DTSTART`. A bare date (`2026-04-18`) is all-day; a timestamp (`2026-04-18T14:00:00Z`) is an instant |
| `end` | both | same value types as `start`; omitted when a single all-day item |
| `group` | both | a name, resolved through `groups.md` |
| `stage` | `task` only | `todo` / `doing` / `done`. Replaces the old `done` boolean |
| `priority` | `task` only | `PRIORITY`. The UI writes 1-3; 1-9 is read and bucketed into the three |
| `estimate` | `task` only | days. Ours, no RFC 5545 equivalent |
| `location` | both | free text |
| `alerts` | both | minutes before start, `0` = at start. Stored and exported only; nothing fires in the background |
| `participants` | both | list of email addresses |
| `recurrence` | both | RRULE string, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SA` |
| `exdate` / `rdate` | recurring | occurrences to skip / extra occurrences |
| `status` | override | `cancelled` removes the occurrence. The only value used |
| `series` | override | id of the recurring file it belongs to |
| `recurrence-id` | override | the original occurrence date this file replaces |
| `conflictOf` | conflict file | written by sync |

No `duration` key — it is `end - start`.

Type and time are independent: `type` decides whether the entry has a stage, a priority and an
estimate, the value type of `start` decides whether it is all-day or timed. A task is usually
all-day, but may carry a time and then renders at it.

`stage` is a task's only progress field; there is no `done` key any more. A file written before
the change, or by hand, is read for `done` as a fallback: `done: true` is stage `done`, anything
else is `todo`. Nothing rewrites such a file until it is edited, and a write never emits `done`.

`status` is deliberately *not* the stage field. It already means cancellation on an override,
and one key cannot carry both without an override's cancellation reading as a kanban column.

The bare-date form matters. An all-day task stored as `2026-04-18T00:00:00Z` lands on the wrong
day outside UTC and shifts twice a year on DST.

94	    else if (e.name.endsWith('.md')) {
95	      // isTruncated means text is unusable; fetch that one path over REST instead.
96	      out.push({ path, oid: e.object.oid, text: e.object.text, truncated: !!e.object.isTruncated });
97	    }
98	  }
99	}
100	
101	// ---- pull: 304-guarded, fetches only what changed ----
102	
103	export async function pull(prefix = '') {
104	  const c = await auth();
105	  const etag = await getKV('commitEtag');
106	  const r = await rest(`/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/commits/${c.branch}`,
107	    { config: c, headers: etag ? { 'If-None-Match': etag } : {} });
108	  if (r.status === 304) return { changed: 0, unchanged: true };
109	  if (r.status === 409) return { changed: 0, empty: true };
110	  await ok(r, 'commit check');
111	  await setKV('commitEtag', r.headers.get('ETag'));
112	
113	  const tree = await ok(await rest(
114	    `/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/trees/${c.branch}?recursive=1`, { config: c }), 'tree read');
115	  if (tree.truncated) throw new SyncError('Tree listing truncated - repo too large for a flat pull.');
116	
117	  const remote = new Map(tree.tree
118	    .filter(t => t.type === 'blob' && t.path.endsWith('.md') && t.path.startsWith(prefix))
119	    .map(t => [t.path, t.sha]));
120	  const local = new Map((await allFiles(prefix)).map(f => [f.path, f.oid]));
121	
122	  let changed = 0;
123	  for (const [path, sha] of remote) {
124	    if (local.get(path) === sha) continue;
125	    const blob = await ok(await rest(`/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/blobs/${sha}`, { config: c }), 'blob read');
126	    await putFile({ path, text: decode(blob.content), oid: sha });
127	    changed++;
128	  }
129	  for (const path of local.keys()) if (!remote.has(path)) { await delFile(path); changed++; }
130	  return { changed };
131	}
132	
133	// ---- writes: queue locally, drain as one atomic commit ----
134	
135	export async function write(path, text) {
136	  const existing = await getFile(path);
137	  await putFile({ path, text, oid: existing?.oid });
138	  await enqueue({ op: 'put', path, text, baseOid: existing?.oid ?? null });
139	}
140	
141	export async function remove(path) {
142	  const existing = await getFile(path);
143	  await delFile(path);
144	  await enqueue({ op: 'del', path, baseOid: existing?.oid ?? null });
145	}
146	
147	export async function drain(message, retry = true) {
148	  const items = await queued();
149	  if (!items.length) return { committed: 0, conflicts: [] };
150	  const c = await auth();
151	
152	  let parent = null, baseTree = null;
153	  const refRes = await rest(`/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/ref/heads/${c.branch}`, { config: c });
154	  const fresh = refRes.status === 409 || refRes.status === 404;   // empty repo: no ref yet
155	  if (fresh) return initialise(c, items, message, retry);
156	
157	  parent = (await ok(refRes, 'ref read')).object.sha;
158	  baseTree = (await ok(await rest(
159	    `/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/commits/${parent}`, { config: c }), 'commit read')).tree.sha;
160	
161	  // A queued change whose base SHA no longer matches the remote blob is a real conflict:
162	  // remote keeps the path, ours is committed beside it. Nothing is discarded.
163	  const conflicts = [];
164	  {
165	    const tree = await ok(await rest(
166	      `/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/trees/${c.branch}?recursive=1`, { config: c }), 'tree read');
167	    const remote = new Map(tree.tree.filter(t => t.type === 'blob').map(t => [t.path, t.sha]));
168	    const stamp = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10).replace(/-/g, '');
169	    for (const it of items) {
170	      const live = remote.get(it.path);
171	      if (!it.baseOid || !live || live === it.baseOid) continue;
172	      const blob = await ok(await rest(`/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/blobs/${live}`, { config: c }), 'blob read');
173	      await putFile({ path: it.path, text: decode(blob.content), oid: live });  // theirs wins the path
174	      const original = it.path;
175	      it.path = original.replace(/\.md$/, `.conflict-${stamp}.md`);
176	      if (it.op === 'put') {
177	        const { data, body } = parse(it.text);
178	        it.text = serialize({ ...data, conflictOf: original }, body);
179	      }
180	      conflicts.push({ path: original, keptAs: it.path });
181	    }
182	  }
183	
184	  const entries = [];
185	  for (const it of items) {
186	    if (it.op === 'del') { entries.push({ path: it.path, mode: '100644', type: 'blob', sha: null }); continue; }
187	    const blob = await ok(await rest(`/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/blobs`,
188	      { config: c, method: 'POST', body: { content: encode(it.text), encoding: 'base64' } }), 'blob create');
189	    entries.push({ path: it.path, mode: '100644', type: 'blob', sha: blob.sha, _text: it.text });
190	  }
191	
192	  const tree = await ok(await rest(`/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/trees`, {
193	    config: c, method: 'POST',
194	    body: { base_tree: baseTree, tree: entries.map(strip) }
195	  }), 'tree create');
196	
197	  const commit = await ok(await rest(`/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/commits`, {
198	    config: c, method: 'POST',
199	    body: { message: message || `${items.length} change(s) from Mine`, tree: tree.sha, parents: [parent] }
200	  }), 'commit create');
201	
202	  {
203	    const r = await rest(`/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/git/refs/heads/${c.branch}`, {
204	      config: c, method: 'PATCH', body: { sha: commit.sha, force: false }
205	    });
206	    if (!r.ok) {
207	      // Rejected: someone pushed elsewhere. Rebase onto the new base and retry once -
208	      // this succeeds because nearly every write is a create at a fresh path.
209	      if (retry && (r.status === 422 || r.status === 409)) { await pull(); return drain(message, false); }
210	      await ok(r, 'ref update');
211	    }
212	  }
213	
214	  for (const e of entries) {
215	    if (e.sha === null) await delFile(e.path);
216	    else await putFile({ path: e.path, text: e._text, oid: e.sha });
217	  }
218	  await clearQueue();
219	  await setKV('commitEtag', null);   // our own commit changed the ref
220	  return { committed: items.length, commit: commit.sha, conflicts };
221	}
222	
223	const strip = ({ _text, ...e }) => e;
224	
225	// A repo with no commits rejects the Git Data API outright: POST /git/blobs answers
226	// 409 "Git Repository is empty". Only the Contents API can create the first commit, so the
227	// first queued file goes that way and the rest drain normally once a history exists.
228	async function initialise(c, items, message, retry) {
229	  const first = items.find(i => i.op === 'put');
230	  if (!first) { await clearQueue(); return { committed: 0, conflicts: [] }; }
231	
232	  const res = await ok(await rest(`/repos/${c.owner}/${c.repo}/contents/${encodeURI(first.path)}`, {
233	    config: c, method: 'PUT',
234	    body: {
235	      message: message || 'Initial commit from Mine',
236	      content: encode(first.text),
237	      branch: c.branch
238	    }
239	  }), 'initial commit');
240	
241	  await putFile({ path: first.path, text: first.text, oid: res.content.sha });
242	
243	  const rest_ = items.filter(i => i !== first);
244	  await clearQueue();
245	  await setKV('commitEtag', null);
246	  if (!rest_.length) return { committed: 1, commit: res.commit.sha, conflicts: [] };
247	
248	  for (const it of rest_) await enqueue(it);
249	  const more = await drain(message, retry);
250	  return { ...more, committed: more.committed + 1, commit: more.commit || res.commit.sha };
251	}

# Mine — technical requirements

How [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) is built. Everything here was verified against the live
API or on device on 2026-11-19; `spike/` re-runs the device checks and needs no token.

## Repos

| Repo | Visibility | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maximilianharr/mine` | public | this app, served by Pages at `/mine/` |
| `maximilianharr/mine-data` | **private** | the markdown data |

Pages cannot serve a private repo without Enterprise, so data in the app repo would be
world-readable at a predictable URL. The token is scoped to the data repo only.

## Layout

One `manifest.json` with `scope: /mine/`, one service worker at the root. Subfolders are ordinary
pages inside that scope. `/mine/` and `/mine/calendar/` are the same origin, so they share one
IndexedDB — that is the whole mechanism behind "enter the token once".

```
/index.html /manifest.json /sw.js
/shared/  apps.js  store.js  github.js  md.js  vendor/
/calendar/  index.html  app.js  widget.js  icon.svg  sample/
```

No build step: no bundler, no CI, no node_modules. `git push` deploys, every page opens from
disk, all paths relative so the `/mine/` prefix needs no config.

`shared/apps.js` exports the app list and is imported by both the tile screen and `sw.js`, so
adding an app means editing one array. An app may export `summary()` from `widget.js`.

## Bootstrap — 1 request

One GraphQL query returns an app folder's tree **with contents and blob SHAs**, nested to the
depth of the layout:

```graphql
repository(owner:$o, name:$r) { object(expression:"main:calendar") {
  ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
    ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
      ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
        ... on Blob { oid text isTruncated } } } } } } } } } } }
```

- `rateLimit.cost` is **1** however many files return — `entries` is not a paginated connection.
  A 16 MB / 145 file response came back in 6 s without error.
- `Blob.oid` is byte-identical to the REST tree SHA, so this single request also supplies the
  SHAs that pulls diff against and writes send as their base.
- Check `isTruncated`: GraphQL truncates very large blobs and returns `text: null` for binary.
  Fall back to a REST blob fetch for that path.
- An **empty repo** returns `object: null` rather than an error, and `defaultBranchRef: null`.
  Treat it as an empty mirror, not a failure.

**Do not use the tarball.** `GET /tarball/{ref}` 302-redirects to `codeload.github.com`, which
answers `access-control-allow-origin: https://render.githubusercontent.com` — one specific
foreign origin. `fetch()` applies CORS to the final response after the redirect, so it is
blocked, and the preflight an authenticated request needs returns 403. `api.github.com/graphql`
by contrast sends `allow-origin: *` and a 204 preflight allowing `Authorization`.

**A repo with no commits rejects the Git Data API outright.** Not just the ref read — `POST
/git/blobs` itself answers 409 "Git Repository is empty", so there is nothing to build a tree
from. Only `PUT /contents/{path}` can create the first commit. The first queued file goes that
way, and everything after drains normally once a history exists.

## Pull

1. `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{branch}` with `If-None-Match`. A 304 means nothing changed and
   costs no rate-limit quota.
2. On 200: fetch the tree, diff blob SHAs, fetch only changed files, drop deleted paths.

Run on app open and on window focus. Background Sync does not exist in Safari, so all syncing is
foreground.

## Writes — one commit per drain

Queue each change locally with the blob SHA it was based on, then drain the whole queue as one
commit via the Git Data API: `POST /git/blobs` per file, `POST /git/trees` with `base_tree`
(deletion = entry with `sha: null`), `POST /git/commits`, `PATCH /git/refs/heads/{branch}` with
the expected old SHA and **no force**.

One drain is one commit, so a move — delete plus create, because the date is in the path and the
API has no rename — cannot be half-applied, and a 20-item offline backlog is one commit.

A rejected ref update means someone pushed elsewhere: pull, rebuild on the new base, retry. This
succeeds, because nearly every write is a create at a freshly generated path.

**True conflict** = a queued change whose base SHA no longer matches the remote blob. Remote keeps
the canonical path; the local version is committed beside it as `<name>.conflict-<yyyymmdd>.md`
with `conflictOf:`. Nothing is discarded and the queue never jams. On 401/403, pause and send the
user to settings.

## Service worker

Registered `{type: 'module'}` so it can import `shared/apps.js`. A version constant names the
cache; install precaches the shell. Same-origin requests are cache-then-revalidate.

Requests to `api.github.com` **bypass the worker entirely** — caching an API response would hand
back a stale ETag and silently break sync.

A new worker waits; the UI offers "Update ready — reload" and `skipWaiting()` runs only on tap.

## Token and CSP

Stored plaintext in IndexedDB with its expiry: as safe as the unlocked device. The threat that
matters is injected script on our own origin, closed off by policy rather than encryption:

```
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com
```

**No CDNs, ever.** Dependencies are committed to `/shared/vendor/`, pinned by hand, with source
URL and version in `VENDOR.md`. The token is never written to a log, a URL, or the DOM.

The OAuth device flow is not an option: GitHub's `login/device/code` endpoints send no CORS
headers, so a fine-grained PAT is the only no-backend path.

## Dependencies

| What | Why not hand-rolled |
| --- | --- |
| `js-yaml` | Files are hand-edited and must parse as real YAML — quoting, multiline scalars, flow maps. A subset parser misreads them silently. |
| `rrule` | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR` and DST-crossing weeklies are where hand-rolled expansion is wrong without telling you. |

YAML *writing* is ours (~20 lines): we control the output shape, so no dumper is needed.

**Load with `CORE_SCHEMA`, never js-yaml's default.** The default is YAML 1.1 and parses
`start: 2026-04-18` into a JS Date at UTC midnight — silently shifting every all-day entry by a
day east of UTC. `CORE_SCHEMA` keeps it a string and still handles bools, numbers, flow maps and
quoted scalars. This is the same off-by-one the bare-date format exists to prevent, arriving
through the parser instead.

## Platform findings

Verified in both installed home-screen apps (iPhone/Safari, Pixel/Chrome); screenshots in
`spike/res/`.

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Storage shared across paths | **Yes.** A marker written by `/mine/spike/` was read back byte-identical by `/mine/spike/sub/`, both reporting `STANDALONE`. Cross-path module imports work too. |
| `{type:'module'}` service worker | Registers on Safari as well as Chrome. No classic fallback needed. |
| `storage.persisted()` | **Already granted**, no prompt, on both. An installed app is exempt from the ~7-day eviction that applies to uninstalled sites, so the token and mirror survive idle periods. |
| Quota | 35 GB (iPhone), 56 GB (Pixel), against a mirror measured in single-digit MB. |

Not tested, and no longer relevant: whether separately-installed PWAs get isolated storage. That
expectation is why the one-app topology was chosen.

Re-run `spike/` after a major iOS release — two of the four results above contradicted the
documented platform behaviour, and that is exactly the kind of thing that regresses silently.

content.content:
1	# Calendar
2	
3	Calendar is an app of [Mine](../REQUIREMENTS.md) to manage your calendar. Every entry is one
4	markdown file in the data repo, so your calendar stays readable and portable without this app.
5	
6	See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for the file format.
7	
8	## What an entry holds
9	
10	A title, a type — **event** or **task** — a start and end, a group, a location, participants,
11	alerts, and a free markdown body for the agenda, checklist or notes.
12	
13	A task also carries a **stage** — `todo`, `doing` or `done` — and, optionally, a priority (1, 2
14	or 3) and an estimate in days. An event has none of the three. Stage is the only record of a
15	task's progress; there is no separate done flag.
16	
17	Entries can repeat, and a repeating entry can have single occurrences skipped, moved, retitled

# Calendar

Calendar is an app of [Mine](../REQUIREMENTS.md) to manage your calendar. Every entry is one
markdown file in the data repo, so your calendar stays readable and portable without this app.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for the file format.

## What an entry holds

A title, a type — **event** or **task** — a start and end, a group, a location, participants,
alerts, and a free markdown body for the agenda, checklist or notes.

A task also carries a **stage** — `todo`, `doing` or `done` — and, optionally, a priority (1, 2
or 3) and an estimate in days. An event has none of the three. Stage is the only record of a
task's progress; there is no separate done flag.

Entries can repeat, and a repeating entry can have single occurrences skipped, moved, retitled
or moved to another stage without affecting the rest.

## Layout

A navigation pane at the top and a big calendar window below it.

In the top pane, from left to right:

- Left/right buttons to move to the previous/next day, week, month, year or sprint, depending on
  the current view.
- The current day/week/month/year, with a small downward arrow for a dropdown date picker. The
  dropdown shows a month at a time, with its name top left and left/right arrows top right.
  Clicking the month name switches to a year grid of 9 years ending with the current one, whose
  arrows page by 9 years. In the kanban view the label reads `Sprint 7 · 19 Jan – 1 Feb` and the
  dropdown picks a sprint.
- A button to jump to today.
- A dropdown to filter by group. Each group shows its colour. This is a view filter and is
  remembered per device; groups are *named and coloured* in settings, not here.
- `D` `W` `M` `Y` `K` to choose the view: day, week, month, year, kanban.
- A return arrow back to the Mine tile screen.
- A gear button that opens settings.

All views show **seven columns beginning with the configured first day of the week**, with
Saturday and Sunday tinted wherever they land. A Saturday task has to be visible.

When *show calendar weeks* is on, each week row carries its ISO 8601 week number in a left
gutter, separated from the days by a thin vertical rule. The number is always ISO, whichever
day the week is set to start on.

A `+` button adds an entry. It defaults to today when today is in view, and otherwise to the
first day on screen — in the kanban, to the first day of the selected sprint, in its todo
column.

## Views

- **Year** — every month, each with a weekday header row and one row per week. The current day
  is highlighted. A day with entries takes the background colour of its group, split between
  colours if there are several — a year grid has no room for anything else. Clicking a day shows
  that day's entries.
- **Month** — one row per week. Entries appear inside each day cell as small lines carrying the
  title on the group's background colour, sorted by time, all-day items first. A cell shows at
  most four on desktop and two on a phone, then `+N`. Tasks have a rectangular icon on the right
  to move them straight to done. Clicking empty space in a cell creates an entry; clicking an
  entry opens it.
- **Week** — columns are the days, rows are the 24 hours.
- **Day** — the week view for a single day, with more detail per entry.
- **Kanban** — below.

Groups switched off in the filter are not shown in any view.

### The day preview

Clicking a day opens that day's entries as a list, each one tappable. Its top right carries a
small `+` to add an entry on that day and a small `x` to close it — not full-width buttons.

## Entry popup

A row of icon buttons at the top, from left to right:

- `T` for task, `E` for event. Choosing one deselects the other; the default is event.
- A circular-arrows button for **repetition**.
- A ball for **category**.
- A pin for **location**.
- A bell for **alerts**.
- A person for **participants**.
- `D` for **details** — the markdown body.
- Then, right-aligned: an `x` to close and discard, a trashcan to delete the entry, and a disk
  to save it.

An icon whose field is set is shown enabled: a brighter background in dark mode, a darker one in
light mode. So the row doubles as a summary of what the entry carries.

Each of the seven field buttons opens its own popup, and every popup has the same three buttons:
a trashcan that clears that one field, an `x` that abandons the sub-edit, and a disk that commits
the value into the entry form and lights the icon. **A sub-popup never writes to the repo.**
Nothing is written until the entry popup's own disk, so one entry edit is one commit, and the
entry popup's `x` discards the staged fields along with everything else. This is also what makes
a brand-new entry work, since it has no file for a sub-popup to write to.

Below the icon row:

- the title field;
- for a task, a `todo` / `doing` / `done` button group;
- the start and end fields;
- then one row per field that is set, in the order of the icons above — so a location that has
  been given appears at the bottom. Each row has a pen to reopen its popup and a trashcan to
  clear it.

Saving **closes the popup and returns to the calendar immediately**; the push to GitHub runs in
the background and is reported in the sync line, not in the popup.

### Repetition

A dropdown, not an RRULE field:

```
does not repeat · daily · weekly · every 2 weeks ·
monthly on the x-th · monthly on the x-th weekday · yearly
```

below it an **ends** control: never, on a date, or after a number of occurrences.

Files may be hand-written or imported, so a rule the dropdown cannot express — `the last Friday
of the month`, `Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays` — is shown as a non-selectable **custom** state
displaying the rule as text, with a note that choosing an option will replace it. Saving the
entry without touching the dropdown leaves the rule untouched. No hand-written rule is ever
silently rewritten.

### Category

The groups, each with its colour, and a `+ add` button. Adding a group asks for a label and a
colour; its stored name is derived from the label and never shown, which is why relabelling or
recolouring later touches no entry. A pen edits a group, a trashcan deletes it — and entries
still naming a deleted group render grey.

## Kanban

Three columns — **todo** (red), **doing** (yellow), **done** (green) — holding one sprint's
tasks. Every task is a card and every card is a task; events never appear.

A sprint is a date range, not a stored field: sprint 1 starts on the *kanban first week start
date* and each one runs for the *kanban interval*. A task's sprint is whichever range its start
falls in, so the number can never disagree with the date, and moving a card to another sprint
is exactly a change of its start and end. Both settings therefore live in the data repo, not on
the device — if they differed between two devices the same card would be in different sprints.

A repeating task contributes one card per occurrence inside the sprint. Moving one records an
override for that occurrence alone; the rule itself is never rewritten.

Each column header shows its state, its colour and a card count. The sprint selector and a
filter icon (category, assignee, priority) sit in the top pane, because one board shows one
sprint.

A card shows:

- a top row with a trashcan to delete, a pen to edit, the title, and `<` `>` to move it to the
  previous or next stage — `<` disabled in todo, `>` disabled in done;
- below it two lines of the markdown body;
- on the right a priority chip (1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow), the estimate in days, and the sprint
  number. Clicking any of the three changes it; changing the sprint moves the task's start and
  end to that sprint's range.

On desktop all three columns are shown and a card can be dragged between them. On a phone one
column fills the screen, swiping sideways moves between them, and the `<` `>` buttons on each
card do the moving — so the swipe never has to be told apart from a drag. Cards are not
reordered by hand; their order comes from priority and start.

## Settings

The gear button opens a panel whose top right has an `x` to close:

- **Groups** — the list of groups, each with its colour, a pen to edit and a `+` to add.
- **Start week on** — Monday or Sunday.
- **Time zone** — a zone name such as `Europe/Berlin`, defaulting to the device's own. A plain
  `UTC+1` is not offered: it is an hour wrong for half the year in any zone with daylight saving.
- **Date format** — `auto` (the device's locale), `dd.mm.yyyy` or `mm/dd/yy`.
- **Show calendar weeks**.
- **Kanban interval** — in weeks.
- **Kanban first week start date**.
- **Theme** — system, light or dark.

Everything here is stored on the device except the groups, the kanban interval and the kanban
first week start date, which are data and live in the repo so they follow you and mean the same
thing everywhere. Theme and date format apply to all of Mine, not the calendar alone, and the
main app's settings shows the same two rows.

## On a phone

The views above describe the desktop. The same screens adapt:

- The top pane collapses to `[<] [April 2026 v] [D W M Y K] [←] [⚙]`.
- A month cell shows at most two entry lines, then `+N`; a year cell stays a coloured day.
- Tapping a day opens that day's entries as a sheet, each one tappable, with the small `+` and
  `x` in its top right — so nothing is ever smaller than a finger.
- The kanban shows one column at a time.

## On the main screen

The tile screen of the main app shows today's entries and the next one coming up.

1	# Calendar — technical requirements
2	
3	File format and rendering for [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md). Sync, caching and writes are
4	in [../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md).
5	
6	## Paths
7	
8	```
9	calendar/2026/04/2026-04-18-1400-k3f9.md     one-off entry
10	calendar/2026/04/2026-04-25-0000-ov1q.md     occurrence override
11	calendar/recurring/trash-p7qm.md             entry with a recurrence rule
12	calendar/groups.md                           group -> colour and label
13	calendar/settings.md                         kanban anchor and interval
14	```
15	
16	The whole folder is mirrored locally, so the path is not a loading optimisation. It is for
17	humans: the repo browses chronologically on github.com, and no directory grows past a month of
18	entries. `-k3f9` is 4 random characters, **not** a counter — two devices creating entries offline
19	on the same day must never mint the same name. No title slug, so retitling is never a rename.
20	
21	**The path is never the source of truth.** It is derived from `start` at creation; after a move
22	or an override the two can disagree. Always read `start`. Changing an entry's date is a rename,
23	which is a delete plus a create in one commit.
24	
25	Entries with a `recurrence:` rule live in `recurring/` rather than the date tree, because an
26	open-ended rule must render in months it was not created in and there is no month folder to find
27	it under.
28	
29	## Frontmatter
30	
31	RFC 5545 (iCalendar) naming wherever one exists, so `.ics` export is close to a field copy.
32	**Empty keys are omitted, never written as `None`** — `None` is a YAML string, not null, and a
33	parser hands back the text `"None"`.
34	
35	| Key | Applies to | Notes |
36	| --- | --- | --- |
37	| `title` | both | required |
38	| `type` | both | `event` or `task` |
39	| `start` | both | `DTSTART`. A bare date (`2026-04-18`) is all-day; a timestamp (`2026-04-18T14:00:00Z`) is an instant |
40	| `end` | both | same value types as `start`; omitted when a single all-day item |
41	| `group` | both | a name, resolved through `groups.md` |
42	| `stage` | `task` only | `todo` / `doing` / `done`. Replaces the old `done` boolean |
43	| `priority` | `task` only | `PRIORITY`. The UI writes 1-3; 1-9 is read and bucketed into the three |
44	| `estimate` | `task` only | days. Ours, no RFC 5545 equivalent |
45	| `location` | both | free text |
46	| `alerts` | both | minutes before start, `0` = at start. Stored and exported only; nothing fires in the background |
47	| `participants` | both | list of email addresses |
48	| `recurrence` | both | RRULE string, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SA` |
49	| `exdate` / `rdate` | recurring | occurrences to skip / extra occurrences |
50	| `status` | override | `cancelled` removes the occurrence. The only value used |
51	| `series` | override | id of the recurring file it belongs to |
52	| `recurrence-id` | override | the original occurrence date this file replaces |
53	| `conflictOf` | conflict file | written by sync |
54	
55	No `duration` key — it is `end - start`.
56	
57	Type and time are independent: `type` decides whether the entry has a stage, a priority and an
58	estimate, the value type of `start` decides whether it is all-day or timed. A task is usually
59	all-day, but may carry a time and then renders at it.
60	
61	`stage` is a task's only progress field; there is no `done` key any more. A file written before
62	the change, or by hand, is read for `done` as a fallback: `done: true` is stage `done`, anything
63	else is `todo`. Nothing rewrites such a file until it is edited, and a write never emits `done`.
64	
65	`status` is deliberately *not* the stage field. It already means cancellation on an override,
66	and one key cannot carry both without an override's cancellation reading as a kanban column.
67	
68	The bare-date form matters. An all-day task stored as `2026-04-18T00:00:00Z` lands on the wrong
69	day outside UTC and shifts twice a year on DST.
70	
71	The markdown body is the entry's content and is preserved byte-for-byte by anything that does not
72	explicitly edit it.
73	
74	## Overrides
75	
76	A recurring file states the rule only. Anything that happens to a *single* occurrence — ticked,
77	moved, retitled, cancelled — is an override file in the date tree carrying `series:` and
78	`recurrence-id:`, holding only the keys that differ. The rule file is never rewritten, and since
79	each override is a fresh path it cannot conflict, even when two devices do it offline.
80	
81	`exdate:` covers a plain skip where there is nothing to record.
82	
83	## Rendering a range
84	
85	1. Collect dated entries whose `start` falls in the range.
86	2. Expand every rule in `recurring/` over the range; drop dates in `exdate`, add `rdate`.
87	3. Replace an occurrence with the override matching `series` + `recurrence-id`; an override
88	   marked cancelled removes it.
89	4. Drop groups switched off in the filter.
90	5. Sort: all-day first, then by start time.
91	
92	Index overrides by `` `${series}|${recurrenceId}` `` once per load; a linear scan per occurrence
93	is what makes month views slow.
94	
95	## RRULE
96	
97	Full RRULE on read — files may be hand-written or imported. The UI *writes* only the seven
98	shapes its dropdown offers, plus the ends control:
99	
100	| Dropdown | Written |
101	| --- | --- |
102	| does not repeat | key omitted |
103	| daily | `FREQ=DAILY` |
104	| weekly | `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=<start's weekday>` |
105	| every 2 weeks | `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=<start's weekday>` |
106	| monthly on the x-th | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=<x>` |
107	| monthly on the x-th weekday | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=<n><DD>` |
108	| yearly | `FREQ=YEARLY` |
109	| ends on a date | `+UNTIL=<date>Z` |
110	| ends after n | `+COUNT=<n>` |
111	
112	Anything the dropdown cannot round-trip to one of those is held as **custom**: displayed as
113	text, not editable, and written back byte-for-byte unless the user picks a dropdown value. The
114	test is round-tripping, not parsing — `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR` parses fine and is still custom,
115	because no dropdown entry regenerates it.
116	
117	`rrule.js` works in UTC. For an all-day rule, set `DTSTART` to UTC midnight and read only the
118	year/month/day back, never `getDate()` on a local Date — east of UTC that returns the previous
119	day. `UNTIL` must be written in the `Z` form.
120	
121	## Groups
122	
123	`groups.md` is a markdown file whose frontmatter maps a group name to a colour and a label. An
124	entry stores the name, so recolouring or relabelling is a one-file edit instead of a rewrite of
125	every entry, and there is no cap on the number of groups. Unknown group renders grey. It lives in
126	the data repo, so the mapping follows you across devices.
127	
128	## Settings
129	
130	Two of the settings are data, not preferences, and live in `calendar/settings.md`:
131	
132	```yaml
133	---
134	kanban-anchor: 2026-01-05     # bare date: the first day of sprint 1
135	kanban-interval: 2            # weeks
136	---
137	```
138	
139	They are in the repo because the sprint a task belongs to is *derived* from them. On the device
140	they would make the same file report a different sprint on a phone than on a laptop, and moving
141	a card would then write the wrong date. Everything else — theme, date format, time zone, week
142	start, show-calendar-weeks, the group filter — is a device preference in IndexedDB, the group
143	filter under `calendar.hiddenGroups` as it already is. Theme and date format are Mine-wide keys,
144	not the calendar's.
145	
146	## Sprints
147	
148	There is no `sprint` key. Sprint *n* runs from `anchor + (n-1) × interval` weeks for `interval`
149	weeks, and a task's sprint is whichever range its `start` falls in. So:
150
