# Calendar — technical requirements

File format and rendering for [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md). Sync, caching and writes are
in [../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Paths

```
calendar/2026/04/2026-04-18-1400-k3f9.md     one-off entry
calendar/2026/04/2026-04-25-0000-ov1q.md     occurrence override
calendar/recurring/trash-p7qm.md             entry with a recurrence rule
calendar/groups.md                           group -> colour and label
calendar/settings.md                         kanban anchor and interval
```

The whole folder is mirrored locally, so the path is not a loading optimisation. It is for
humans: the repo browses chronologically on github.com, and no directory grows past a month of
entries. `-k3f9` is 4 random characters, **not** a counter — two devices creating entries offline
on the same day must never mint the same name. No title slug, so retitling is never a rename.

**The path is never the source of truth.** It is derived from `start` at creation; after a move
or an override the two can disagree. Always read `start`. Changing an entry's date is a rename,
which is a delete plus a create in one commit.

Entries with a `recurrence:` rule live in `recurring/` rather than the date tree, because an
open-ended rule must render in months it was not created in and there is no month folder to find
it under.

## Frontmatter

RFC 5545 (iCalendar) naming wherever one exists, so `.ics` export is close to a field copy.
**Empty keys are omitted, never written as `None`** — `None` is a YAML string, not null, and a
parser hands back the text `"None"`.

| Key | Applies to | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | both | required |
| `type` | both | `event` or `task` |
| `start` | both | `DTSTART`. A bare date (`2026-04-18`) is all-day; a timestamp (`2026-04-18T14:00:00Z`) is an instant |
| `end` | both | same value types as `start`; omitted when a single all-day item |
| `group` | both | a name, resolved through `groups.md` |
| `stage` | `task` only | `todo` / `doing` / `done`. Replaces the old `done` boolean |
| `priority` | `task` only | `PRIORITY`. The UI writes 1-3; 1-9 is read and bucketed into the three |
| `estimate` | `task` only | days. Ours, no RFC 5545 equivalent |
| `location` | both | free text |
| `alerts` | both | minutes before start, `0` = at start. Stored and exported only; nothing fires in the background |
| `participants` | both | list of email addresses |
| `recurrence` | both | RRULE string, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SA` |
| `exdate` / `rdate` | recurring | occurrences to skip / extra occurrences |
| `status` | override | `cancelled` removes the occurrence. The only value used |
| `series` | override | id of the recurring file it belongs to |
| `recurrence-id` | override | the original occurrence date this file replaces |
| `conflictOf` | conflict file | written by sync |

No `duration` key — it is `end - start`.

Type and time are independent: `type` decides whether the entry has a stage, a priority and an
estimate, the value type of `start` decides whether it is all-day or timed. A task is usually
all-day, but may carry a time and then renders at it.

`stage` is a task's only progress field; there is no `done` key any more. A file written before
the change, or by hand, is read for `done` as a fallback: `done: true` is stage `done`, anything
else is `todo`. Nothing rewrites such a file until it is edited, and a write never emits `done`.

`status` is deliberately *not* the stage field. It already means cancellation on an override,
and one key cannot carry both without an override's cancellation reading as a kanban column.

The bare-date form matters. An all-day task stored as `2026-04-18T00:00:00Z` lands on the wrong
day outside UTC and shifts twice a year on DST.

The markdown body is the entry's content and is preserved byte-for-byte by anything that does not
explicitly edit it.

## Overrides

A recurring file states the rule only. Anything that happens to a *single* occurrence — ticked,
moved, retitled, cancelled — is an override file in the date tree carrying `series:` and
`recurrence-id:`, holding only the keys that differ. The rule file is never rewritten, and since
each override is a fresh path it cannot conflict, even when two devices do it offline.

`exdate:` covers a plain skip where there is nothing to record.

## Rendering a range

1. Collect dated entries whose `start` falls in the range.
2. Expand every rule in `recurring/` over the range; drop dates in `exdate`, add `rdate`.
3. Replace an occurrence with the override matching `series` + `recurrence-id`; an override
   marked cancelled removes it.
4. Drop groups switched off in the filter.
5. Sort: all-day first, then by start time.

Index overrides by `` `${series}|${recurrenceId}` `` once per load; a linear scan per occurrence
is what makes month views slow.

## RRULE

Full RRULE on read — files may be hand-written or imported. The UI *writes* only the seven
shapes its dropdown offers, plus the ends control:

| Dropdown | Written |
| --- | --- |
| does not repeat | key omitted |
| daily | `FREQ=DAILY` |
| weekly | `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=<start's weekday>` |
| every 2 weeks | `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=<start's weekday>` |
| monthly on the x-th | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=<x>` |
| monthly on the x-th weekday | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=<n><DD>` |
| yearly | `FREQ=YEARLY` |
| ends on a date | `+UNTIL=<date>Z` |
| ends after n | `+COUNT=<n>` |

Anything the dropdown cannot round-trip to one of those is held as **custom**: displayed as
text, not editable, and written back byte-for-byte unless the user picks a dropdown value. The
test is round-tripping, not parsing — `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR` parses fine and is still custom,
because no dropdown entry regenerates it.

`rrule.js` works in UTC. For an all-day rule, set `DTSTART` to UTC midnight and read only the
year/month/day back, never `getDate()` on a local Date — east of UTC that returns the previous
day. `UNTIL` must be written in the `Z` form.

## Groups

`groups.md` is a markdown file whose frontmatter maps a group name to a colour and a label. An
entry stores the name, so recolouring or relabelling is a one-file edit instead of a rewrite of
every entry, and there is no cap on the number of groups. Unknown group renders grey. It lives in
the data repo, so the mapping follows you across devices.

## Settings

Two of the settings are data, not preferences, and live in `calendar/settings.md`:

```yaml
---
kanban-anchor: 2026-01-05     # bare date: the first day of sprint 1
kanban-interval: 2            # weeks
---
```

They are in the repo because the sprint a task belongs to is *derived* from them. On the device
they would make the same file report a different sprint on a phone than on a laptop, and moving
a card would then write the wrong date. Everything else — theme, date format, time zone, week
start, show-calendar-weeks, the group filter — is a device preference in IndexedDB, the group
filter under `calendar.hiddenGroups` as it already is. Theme and date format are Mine-wide keys,
not the calendar's.

## Sprints

There is no `sprint` key. Sprint *n* runs from `anchor + (n-1) × interval` weeks for `interval`
weeks, and a task's sprint is whichever range its `start` falls in. So:

- the number can never contradict the date, because there is only the date;
- moving a card to another sprint is a write of `start` and `end` and nothing else;
- changing the interval renumbers every card at once, which is correct — it is one timeline.

Computed on bare dates in whole days, never through a `Date` at local midnight: the anchor is a
bare date and sprint boundaries must not shift by a day with the viewer's zone. A `start` before
the anchor has no sprint and the card is not on the board.

## Service worker version

The update banner compares versions rather than merely noticing a waiting worker. The worker
answers a `version` message with its `VERSION` constant; the UI shows "Update ready" only when a
waiting worker's version differs from the active one's. `reg.waiting` alone is not the condition
— a byte-identical worker can wait, and then the banner never goes away.

## Widget

`widget.js` exports `summary()`, returning today's entries and the next upcoming one for the main
app's tile screen.

# Mine

Mine is a set of PWAs (Progressive Web Apps) to digitalize ones personal or professional life.
The key idea is to save everything in a repo as markdown files. This can be calendar entries,
diaries, markdowns extracted from voice recordings / pdfs / .. These .md files can easily be
ported to new apps without a vendor lock-in and are processed via an (AI) assistant to help you
plan your day, keep track of tasks, remind you of memories a.k.a. a second brain.

To keep complexity to a minimum each use-case lives in a separate folder. e.g. the calendar PWA
lives completely in a 'calendar' folder as does the zettelkasten and all the other apps. Each
folder contains a 'sample' folder with samples how the markdowns shall look, a REQUIREMENTS.md
describing how the PWA works and a TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md describing how it is built.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for how this is built.

## One app, one setup

Mine installs as **one** app on the phone, with one icon. The apps in the subfolders are pages
inside it, not separate installs.

This is what makes the central requirement work: **the GitHub repo and token are entered once,
in the main app, and every app in a subfolder uses them.** Verified on iPhone and Android.

## Main app

A tile per app: its `icon.svg` above its folder name.

Above the tiles, apps may contribute a summary. The calendar's shows today's entries and the
next one — which matters, because opening the app is the only reminder that works (see below).

## First run

1. Open the app URL and add it to the home screen (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen;
   Android: menu → Install).
2. The setup screen asks for GitHub owner, data repo, branch, and a personal access token.
3. The app tests the connection and reports clearly if it fails.

Settings are stored on the device only. The token is never displayed again after entry, and the
app warns 14 days before it expires.

Two settings belong to Mine rather than to any one app, and the same two rows appear in the main
settings and in each app's: **theme** (system, light or dark) and **date format** (auto, which
follows the device's locale, or `dd.mm.yyyy`, or `mm/dd/yy`). Both default to following the
device, so Mine looks like the rest of the phone until you say otherwise.

## Using it

- Changes appear instantly and are queued for GitHub in the background.
- A sync indicator shows: in sync / pending / error.
- Offline, the queue is kept and sent when you are back online or reopen the app.
- Editing the same entry on two devices never loses either version: the other device's version
  keeps the file, yours is kept beside it and flagged, and the sync indicator tells you there is
  something to review. Nothing is discarded and nothing is silently overwritten — but the app
  does not interrupt you to ask which to keep, because by then you are somewhere else.
- Everything works offline, including dates and search, because the app keeps a full local copy.

## Reminders

**Mine cannot notify you while it is closed.** No browser can schedule a notification for later;
this is a platform limitation, not a missing feature. Alerts are stored with each entry and
exported, and they fire while the app is open. The summary on the tile screen is the reminder.

## Updates

When a new version is deployed the app shows "Update ready — reload". It never updates while you
are in the middle of editing.

The banner appears only when the version waiting to take over genuinely differs from the one
running. A new worker can sit waiting while being identical to the active one, so "a worker is
waiting" is not the test — if it were, the banner would appear on an app with no update at all
and never go away. Reloading twice with no deploy in between must leave no banner.

## Privacy

Your data lives in a **private** repo. The app itself is public, but it contains no data, and the
token is scoped so that it can only touch the data repo.

mkdir -p calendar/sample/2026/04
cat > calendar/sample/2026/04/2026-04-20-0000-t2wv.md <<'EOF'
---
title: "Draft the Q2 hiring plan"
type: task
start: 2026-04-20
stage: doing
priority: 2
estimate: 3
group: work
participants:
  - "jane.doe@example.com"
---

A task carries the three keys an event never has: `stage`, `priority` and `estimate`.

- `stage` is `todo`, `doing` or `done` and is the only record of progress - there is no
  `done` flag.
- `priority` is RFC 5545 `PRIORITY`. The app writes 1, 2 or 3; a hand-written 4-9 is read
  and bucketed into those three.
- `estimate` is in days. It has no RFC 5545 equivalent, so the name is ours.

There is no `sprint` key. The sprint is whichever range in `settings.md` this `start` falls
in, so the number can never disagree with the date, and moving the card to another sprint is
exactly a change of `start`. With the anchor and interval in `sample/settings.md` this one is
in sprint 8, 13-26 April 2026.
EOF
cat > calendar/sample/settings.md <<'EOF'
---
kanban-anchor: 2026-01-05
kanban-interval: 2
---

The two calendar settings that are data rather than preferences.

`kanban-anchor` is a bare date: the first day of sprint 1. `kanban-interval` is the sprint
length in weeks. Sprint *n* therefore runs for `interval` weeks from
`anchor + (n-1) x interval` weeks, and a task's sprint is whichever range its `start` falls
in.

They live in the repo because the sprint is *derived* from them. On the device the same file
would report a different sprint on a phone than on a laptop, and moving a card would then
write the wrong date. Everything else - theme, date format, time zone, week start,
show-calendar-weeks, the group filter - is a device preference and is not in the repo.

A `start` before the anchor has no sprint, and such a task is not on the board.
EOF

content.text: Phone layout is right, and the Monday gutter (14–18) is correct. But the Sunday-start gutter showed 13–17: it was labelling each row with the ISO week of its Sunday, when six of that row's seven days are in the next ISO week. Fixing:

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import io
p = 'calendar/views.js'
s = io.open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
old = """  const grid = el('div', `grid${gut ? ' gut' : ''}`);
  for (let i = 0; i < cells.length; i += 7) {
    if (gut) grid.append(el('span', 'wk', String(isoWeek(cells[i]))));"""
new = """  const grid = el('div', `grid${gut ? ' gut' : ''}`);
  for (let i = 0; i < cells.length; i += 7) {
    // The row's fourth day, not its first. ISO weeks are defined on Monday-start weeks, so a
    // Sunday-start row holds one day of one ISO week and six of the next; the fourth day is in
    // the second either way, which is the number the row reads as.
    if (gut) grid.append(el('span', 'wk', String(isoWeek(addDays(cells[i], 3)))));"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
io.open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s.replace(old, new))
print('gutter now labels each row by its fourth day')
PY

done

aiTitle: Task event popup and calendar fixes

content.text:
Done. Everything in the new requirements is implemented and exercised in a real browser.

**Samples added**

- `calendar/sample/2026/04/2026-04-20-0000-t2wv.md` — a task carrying `stage`, `priority` and `estimate`, with the body explaining the bucketing and why there is no `sprint` key.
- `calendar/sample/settings.md` — `kanban-anchor` / `kanban-interval` and why they're repo data.

**Implemented**

| Area | What landed |
| --- | --- |
| Entry popup | Icon toolbar (T/E, repeat, category, location, alerts, participants, D, then x/trash/disk), lit icons as the summary, detail rows with pen+trash, stage + priority + estimate row, instant close on save |
| Sub-popups | Six field editors; they stage into a draft and never touch the repo |
| Views | D / W / M / Y / K. Month shows titled lines on the group colour (4 desktop / 2 phone, then `+N`); week and day are 24-hour grids with an all-day strip; year is 12 mini-grids with group-coloured days |
| Chrome | ISO week gutter, configurable week start, `+`, filter, return arrow, gear, sprint picker in the date dropdown |
| Kanban | Three columns, per-occurrence cards, priority/estimate/sprint chips, desktop drag, phone swipe + `<`/`>` |
| Settings | All nine rows; groups/interval/anchor to the repo, the rest to the device; theme + date format Mine-wide and mirrored in the main app |
| Update banner | Workers answer a `version` message; the banner needs the versions to **differ** |
| Data | `stage`/`priority`/`estimate` replace `done`, derived sprints, zone-aware placement, writes queue locally and push in the background |

The calendar is now seven modules (`data` `ui` `views` `kanban` `popup` `settings` `app`) plus `shared/prefs.js`; `app.js` went 594 → ~370 lines.

**Verified in headless Chromium** (harnesses are in the scratchpad, nothing in the repo): 0 failures, 0 console errors across desktop and phone widths. Writes were checked by reading back the files — a new task wrote `stage: doing, priority: 2, estimate: 3` with `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO;COUNT=5`; ticking and dropping a recurring occurrence wrote three-key overrides without rewriting the rule; the series edit kept `exdate` and the filename; no write emitted `done:`. A hand-written `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR` showed as non-selectable *custom* and survived a save byte-for-byte. `Pacific/Auckland` put a 22:30Z event at 10:30 the next day. Three reloads with no deploy left no banner; bumping `VERSION` while the page was open produced one.

**Two bugs found by running it:** `textEditor` was a `const` arrow called from the module-level `FIELDS` array (temporal dead zone — the page died on load), and the week gutter labelled each row by its first day, so a Sunday-start row showed the ISO week only one of its seven days belonged to.

**Three things I decided rather than asked** — all now written into the docs:
1. Adding a category from the entry popup writes `groups.md` immediately. It's a different file, and a category shouldn't vanish because you discarded the entry. This is a stated exception to "a sub-popup never writes to the repo".
2. Priority and estimate are editable in the entry popup too — otherwise a task that's never on a board can't get them.
3. The estimate and sprint chips use `prompt()`; only priority cycles. Cycling an estimate would have meant inventing a scale.

**Not done, and not part of this request:** `widget.js` / the tile-screen summary doesn't exist, and alerts still don't fire while the app is open — both predate this change. The docs promise both.
Current branch is `main`, the default branch, so I'll branch first.

Build the calendar's five views, entry popup, kanban and settings

Implements the requirements captured in the /grill-me pass. The calendar had
only a month view; it now has D/W/M/Y/K, an icon-toolbar entry popup, a kanban
board and a settings panel.

Data:
- `stage`/`priority`/`estimate` replace the `done` boolean. A `done:` key is
  still read as a fallback and never written back out.
- Sprints are derived from `kanban-anchor` and `kanban-interval` in
  calendar/settings.md, so the number cannot contradict the date.
- Timed entries are placed in the configured IANA zone rather than the
  device's; bare dates never go near it. Offsets come off the zone's own wall
  clock, in two passes so a time either side of a DST change resolves right.
- Writes only touch the local mirror and the queue; the push runs in the
  background and reports failures and conflicts in the sync line.

UI:
- Month cells carry titled lines on the group colour, capped with +N; week and
  day are 24-hour grids with an all-day strip; year is twelve mini-grids with
  group-coloured days.
- The entry popup's six field icons open sub-popups that stage into a draft.
  Nothing reaches the repo until the popup's own disk, which is what lets a
  brand-new entry work. Adding a category is the one exception, since that is a
  different file.
- The kanban holds one sprint's tasks, one card per occurrence, draggable on
  desktop and swiped between columns on a phone.
- ISO week gutter, configurable week start, group/priority/assignee filter.

Fixes the update banner: the worker now answers a `version` message and the
banner needs the waiting and active versions to differ. `reg.waiting` alone was
true for a byte-identical worker, so the banner never went away.

The calendar is now seven modules plus shared/prefs.js for the two Mine-wide
settings. Verified in headless Chromium at desktop and phone widths: all views
render, writes read back correctly, a hand-written RRULE survives a save
untouched, and three reloads with no deploy leave no banner.
